messages.subject: Re: R GSoC next steps
messages.body_plain:
Mentors:

We have less than a week left to make slot requests to Google.

You need to select both 'Want to Mentor' and each (every) proposed
mentor needs to comment on the proposal(s).

We need your input, and need to see that you are dedicated to your
project ideas, so Toby and I will not consider a project for slotting

if all mentors haven't chimed in on their feelings on the project, and
selected 'want to mentor'.

We also want your input on other project ideas.  Toby and I are not
experts in all areas of computational statistics and applications using
R.  More viewpoints will make it easier to make choices about slots,
and more community interest in a project will potentially make it
easier to give an idea with a shakier proposal a chance to succeed.

Thanks for your participation.

As always, feel free to reach out to me and Toby with any questions.

Regards,

Brian

--
Brian G. Peterson
http://braverock.com/brian/
Ph: 773-459-4973
IM: bgpbraverock

messages.subject: R GSoC 2018 Slotting Projects
messages.body_plain:
Google has given R plenty of slots for our top projects.

I have begun the process of assigning mentors who have selected 'want
to mentor'.

I have also begun the process of *preliminary* slotting of projects
because of the way the project conflict process works.  We've already
lost one promising student to another organization who slotted their
proposal first.

Remember that program rules do not allow us to discuss likelihood of
acceptance or rejection with any of the students.  Google reserves the
right of final approval of slots and notifying students for itself, and
takes a very negative view of organizations that speak out of turn.

I have commented on proposals that look strong, but don't have enough
mentor comments, or enough mentors selecting 'want to mentor'.

Mentors, please review the proposals for your projects to make sure
everything looks OK.  If more information has been requested, please
provide it.  If we need more mentors, lets get it taken care of.  If
you have any issues or questions, please reach out to Toby and me as
soon as possible.

Google will announce accepted and passed-over proposals on April 23rd.

Regards,

Brian

--
Brian G. Peterson
http://braverock.com/brian/
Ph: 773-459-4973
IM: bgpbraverock

messages.subject: R GSoC 2018 message for student applicants
messages.subject_clean: R GSoC 2018 message for student applicants
messages.body_plain:
Students,

We are finalizing the internal review of all your proposals now.  We
received many excellent proposals this year, including multiple
proposals for about half of our proposed projects.

Since we typically only accept one student per project proposal, some
of you will not get slots.

If you have other plans for the summer, e.g. if you expect to take an
internship that would keep you from devoting your full time to GSoC,
please do us and your fellow students a favor over the next few days.

If you will not be able to participate in GSoC, please withdraw your
proposal so that we can give the slot to someone else.

Of course, if you are committed to GSoC, we want you to stick with this
and wait for slot allocations!

If you stay in, get a slot, and then withdraw after slot assignments
are announced, we can't give that slot to another deserving student.
Every year we have a few of these, and every year I wish that the
withdrawing students had been more up-front about their other
commitments with us and GSoC.

Thanks for your attention, and good luck with your GSoC proposals!  We
really did get a good crop of student proposals this year, and you
should be proud of your effort.

Regards,

Brian

--
Brian G. Peterson
http://braverock.com/brian/
Ph: 773-459-4973
IM: bgpbraverock

messages.body_plain:
Mentors:

I've gone through all the proposals and done preliminary starring and
slotting (accepting) of proposals.

Please check my work.

Many of our project ideas received multiple proposals.  I have done my
best to follow your collective lead in slotting the top choice.  Please
make sure that everything looks right to you for your projects.

Also, remember that nothing is final until Google notifies students on
April 23rd. Google program rules do not allow us to discuss likelihood
of acceptance or rejection with any of the students.  Google reserves
the right of final approval of slots and notifying students for itself,
and takes a very negative view of organizations that speak out of turn.

Contact Toby and me immediately if you see something wrong: I slotted
the wrong proposal, I missed a proposal you think is strong enough for
a slot, you have last minute jitters about the proposal, whatever.  We
only have a few more days to finalize things.

Regards,

Brian

--
Brian G. Peterson

> Potential students: now is the time to start contacting mentors for posted ideas, providing patches, submitting test results, etc. to really show your interest in working on an R GSoC project in 2018.  You can even start working on your project application.  The best and most successful student applications typically run to about 10 pages if printed, so it is hard to write the entire thing in the space of the application period.
